message:
chore(release): 0.2.114 -- the first release carrying the client's update check

GNLinkClient.exe grew from 707,584 to 711,168 bytes: that is the wiring that makes
the client ask about updates after a sign-in instead of once, before one was
possible. Windows only; Android untouched.

Verified on a Release rebuild with nothing else building -- 66 suites, 1861
checks, no failures, config and build time recorded alongside. Installer embed
9/9, payload-set gate passed, manifest matched the files 10/10, and the shipped
C++ verifier accepted both the document before publishing and the bytes pulled
back off the server afterwards. Ten public URLs, all 200, all hashing as signed.
No restart, no env change; the 0.2.113 pair is backed up.

manifest-backups has no 0.2.112 and that is correct -- that build existed only to
be installed by hand and was never published.

What this release does NOT fix, and it matters: a host standing down for an update
still leaves its child behind, and that orphan holds the UDP ports the next host
needs. It broke this machine twice today and recovery took the user killing the
process by hand. The fix is the next item and is deliberately not folded in here.
